text: What operation does the classic two-lens 4f optical processor implement on an input image?
choices: Coherent linear spatial filtering: the output is the input convolved with the impulse response of the Fourier-plane mask
A nonlinear thresholding of the image intensity
An optical analog-to-digital conversion of the image
Amplification of the image by stimulated emission
explanation: The first lens Fourier transforms the input, a mask at the Fourier plane multiplies the spectrum, and the second lens inverse-transforms, yielding the input convolved with the mask's impulse response, i.e. any linear translation-invariant operation. It is passive and linear, so it performs no thresholding, no digitization, and provides no gain.
